narrative_purpose: Make the Earth biogeography vivid: the deep sea crowded with light, the land nearly dark — the contrast that sets up the rule the chapter then flips onto Pandora.
subject: A single plate split into two halves joined by darkness. Left half: an Earth deep-sea scene full of glowing life — a lantern-bearing anglerfish, a luminous jellyfish, a counter-illuminating squid, scattered points of blue light throughout the black water. Right half: an Earth forest floor at night, almost entirely dark, with only one small firefly glowing mid-air and a single faint patch of foxfire fungus on a log.
scene: Two natural habitats abutting: open black ocean on the left, dark terrestrial forest floor on the right, the seam between them a band of deep shadow.
camera: A balanced two-panel naturalist composition, each half observed at mid-distance, equal framing.
light: Left: many bioluminescent keys scattered through black water. Right: near-total darkness with one tiny firefly glow and one faint fungal patch — the deliberate scarcity of land glow is the point.
palette: Void-indigo and deep teal throughout both halves; abundant Pandora cyan glow on the sea side, only a scarce amber-green firefly and faint fungal glow on the land side.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture; an honest Earth-science illustration, not a Pandora scene.
detail_level: Crisp on the sea creatures' lights and on the lone land firefly; both backgrounds deep and hazy.
composition: Two equal vertical halves, the bright crowded sea against the dark sparse land, the asymmetry of light between them carrying the meaning.
consistency_notes: Cool palette consistent with the chapter; this plate depicts EARTH, so keep it recognisably terrestrial/oceanic, with land glow conspicuously scarce versus the sea.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
